extracted.intended_audience: federal credit union officials (FICU compliance staff), mortgage servicers, regulatory attorneys, and other stakeholders affected by NCUA share insurance rules
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes the NCUA's final-rule standards for calculating and administering share insurance for trust accounts, mortgage servicer accounts (MSAs), and related recordkeeping and implementation policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust accounts coverage formula
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum coverage for a trust account equals the SMSIA ($250,000) multiplied by the number of grantors multiplied by the number of beneficiaries, up to a maximum of five beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate application: e.g., a single grantor with three beneficiaries yields ($250,000) × (1) × (3) = $750,000. The NCUA emphasizes that a single uniform formula will be used to determine maximum coverage and that this formula does not depend on allocation of funds among beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation across revocable and irrevocable trusts
rubrics_metrics.description: If shares would pass from the same grantor to beneficiaries (even if divided between revocable and irrevocable trust accounts), they are aggregated for purposes of applying the share insurance limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is irrelevant that shares are divided between the living (revocable) trust account and the irrevocable trust account; aggregation can result in reduced coverage relative to current separate-treatment rules. Example: current rules might have insured revocable and irrevocable trusts separately, but under final rule they aggregate for a single grantor limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary cap (maximum of five) for coverage calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of beneficiaries is counted up to a maximum of five when calculating coverage (i.e., insurance is SMSIA × number_of_grantors × min(number_of_beneficiaries, 5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than five beneficiaries are named, the calculation uses five. Under the current rule (prior to this final rule), when more than five beneficiaries are named, the insured amount could be the greater of five times SMSIA or the total of individually-limited beneficiary interests; the final rule simplifies this to the capped formula (example given: seven beneficiaries => use five for calculation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-grantor cap of $1,250,000
rubrics_metrics.description: A single grantor is eligible for a maximum of $1,250,000 for all their trust interests (i.e., SMSIA $250,000 × 5 beneficiaries = $1,250,000 per grantor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board reiterates this applies per grantor (so co-grantors such as a husband and wife could each be eligible for up to $1,250,000). Commenters asked the agency to track liquidations to ensure the cap is appropriate; the agency will monitor uninsured amounts in liquidations if warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merger of revocable and irrevocable trust categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule merges revocable and irrevocable trust account categories into a single trust-accounts category to simplify insurance coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board believes merger will reduce confusion, regulatory burden, and operational complexity. The Board declines to create a formal process to simultaneously calculate coverage under old and new rules for tracking outcomes, but will consider changes if aware of unanticipated decreased coverage via liquidations or public input (in consultation with FDIC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parity with FDIC coverage as policy objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensuring parity between NCUA share insurance and FDIC deposit insurance is an important basis for the changes to trust-account and MSA rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters emphasized parity for consistency and to avoid funds migrating to banks; the NCUA used parity as a guiding principle (e.g., adopting FDIC's approach to MSA principal/interest advances). Parity is an aim but NCUA coverage remains limited to members where statutory limits apply, so exact parallelism is not always possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership eligibility for trust-account insurance
rubrics_metrics.description: NCUA generally provides share insurance only to members; co-owners (settlors) of revocable trust accounts must be members to receive insurance for their interests, whereas joint accounts with a right of survivorship are a statutory exception allowing nonmember co-owners to be insured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCUA's longstanding position: nonmember owners of joint accounts with right of survivorship can be insured if one joint owner is a member (expressly provided in regulations). By contrast, revocable trust co-owners (settlors) are different and must be members under current regulations. For irrevocable trusts, insurance for interests where beneficiaries are members will be based on beneficiaries' membership status even if settlors are not members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of mortgage servicer advances and foreclosure proceeds in MSAs
rubrics_metrics.description: For MSAs consisting of principal and interest payments, cumulative balances used to satisfy principal and interest obligations will be insured up to the SMSIA per mortgagor regardless of whether those funds were paid into the account by the borrower, advanced by the servicer, or are foreclosure proceeds used to satisfy the borrower's obligation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This final rule mirrors an FDIC change: servicer advances to satisfy delinquent borrower obligations are treated as if collected directly from borrowers for coverage purposes. The Board finalized this change and made it effective 30 days after Federal Register publication. The Board also noted inclusion of foreclosure collections in the composition of MSA principal-and-interest balances.

rubrics_metrics.name: MSA tax and insurance escrow accounts treatment unchanged
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate escrow accounts comprised of mortgagors' tax and insurance payments remain insured based on each mortgagor's ownership interest and are aggregated with other funds maintained by the mortgagor at the same FICU in the same right and capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule does not change treatment of tax/insurance escrow funds; they continue to be insured on a pass-through/ownership-interest basis distinct from principal-and-interest MSA treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates for changes (MSA and recordkeeping)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board opted to make the MSA change and the finalized recordkeeping change effective 30 days after publication in the Federal Register; for trust-account rule implementation the Board prefers a substantially delayed effective date (in excess of two years) rather than legacy coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: MSA change expands coverage and imposes no additional burden, so 30-day effective date is appropriate. For trust rules, the Board rejects grandfathering (legacy coverage) due to complexity but will provide a substantially delayed implementation period (matching FDIC's delay) to allow stakeholders time to make adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirements as basis for insurance determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Account records of the FICU are conclusive as to the existence of any relationship (e.g., trustee, agent, custodian, executor) upon which a claim for insurance is founded; if the FICU's records disclose a relationship that may provide a basis for additional insurance, the details and interests must be ascertainable from FICU records or member records maintained in good faith and in the regular course of business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCUA proposed and finalized changes to clarify recordkeeping for accounts maintained by agents, custodians, fiduciaries, or other parties on behalf of a member or beneficial owner; the agency intends these provisions to clearly articulate the records it will look to when evaluating insurance coverage. Finalized change effective 30 days after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications and examples to support implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: NCUA will communicate with FICUs and provide publicly available resources and examples to apprise accountholders of rule changes and to explain how to calculate share insurance coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board agrees it should notify accountholders and remind them to locate necessary trust documents; will communicate with FICUs to ensure examples cover ownership structures implemented by members and to improve understanding/visibility of rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and limited tracking of outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: NCUA will continue to track uninsured amounts in liquidations and monitor potential Share Insurance Fund impacts (e.g., costs), but declines to implement a formal process to simultaneously calculate coverage under current and new trust rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board believes simultaneous calculation would negate simplification benefits; it will monitor liquidations and public input and may consider further changes if aware of unanticipated decreases in coverage or other issues (in consultation with FDIC).
